headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are exposed, but marker can still consume LlamaFactory outputs if manually bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or network surfaces exposed, and marker likewise exposes no shared channel. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste of outputs into marker, so prompt injection is possible only with unusual operator workflow and limited blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies LlamaFactory output into marker as instructions or markup, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added later, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste raw model output into marker prompts.
Use a fixed template for any manual transfer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent has filesystem read/write, clipboard, or network egress, and both profiles show no data classes touched. With no shared workspace or outbound channel, there is no plausible leakage path between LlamaFactory and marker in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access to a shared directory, leakage becomes plausible.
IF either agent is connected to an external API, leakage risk changes.
mitigations: Review any future API integrations before enabling them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles explicitly lack write-capable surfaces: no filesystem write, no git modification, no subprocesses, and no shell. Without overlapping mutable resources, LlamaFactory and marker cannot conflict over state in the documented setup.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF git or database mutation is enabled for both, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Enable locking if mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LlamaFactory can produce model outputs that marker may later ingest, but marker is a document-processing tool and no default action-taking authority is shown. The pathway exists mainly through manual or scripted handoff, so cascading error is possible but the blast radius is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF marker is configured to treat LlamaFactory output as authoritative text, errors can propagate.
IF marker is connected to downstream publishing or automation, impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review before using outputs.
Add a verification step for extracted facts.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, and neither profile indicates residency, retention, or certification constraints. With no documented regulated data flow between LlamaFactory and marker, there is no compliance mismatch to assess from the available evidence.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention policies are added later, reassess.
